Client `<tag>:<verb>` CustomEvents ride a dev-only `EventTarget.prototype.dispatchEvent` wrap (the client runtime's FIRST DOM-prototype wrap — native-apply idiom, capture contained so observability can never break dispatch; the dashed-tag name filter `/^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(?:-[a-z0-9]+)+:./` naturally excludes the framework's internal dot-namespaced events): name/target/timestamp always, `detail` VALUES only behind `settings.inspector.events.captureArgs` — which is server-side-only (`process.gina._inspectorEventsCaptureArgs`), so it reaches the browser via a NEW `__gdGina.inspectorEventsCaptureArgs` whisper in BOTH render delegates (the inspectorUrl/inspectorRedact vehicle — an inspector capture gate that a client surface needs must be whispered; neither the events nor the AI-stream gate reached the client before); captured detail still passes the statusbar redaction walk; capped buffer (200) rides `user.clientEvents` with coalesced publishes; rendered textContent-only below the server events (NO new tab — the 8-tab preset pins stay untouched). Editing inspector SPA/statusbar src is INERT on a live dev inspector until the dist build copies it (served per-request from dist); the inspector tests read dist too — rebuild before the suite.

227. **Upload reset/delete now actually REMOVES the preview + trigger link, restores class-hidden add-affordances, and exposes removal callbacks (#B94/#B95, `0.5.15-alpha.2`).** The validator plugin's `onUploadResetOrDelete` cleanup tail was dead code behind an undefined identifier — `removeListener(gina, $uploadResetTrigger, …)` threw a ReferenceError evaluating its arguments on (nearly) every reset/delete click — so previews and reset links were only inline-HIDDEN, re-uploads accumulated duplicate deterministic trigger ids, and a second cycle could surface a `removeListener` TypeError instead. Fixed by DELETING the ceremony (its de-registration half was a no-op — a fresh anonymous fn was never the registered listener; the native click listener dies with the removed node) and running `$resetLink.remove(); childNodes[i].remove()` directly over a STATIC snapshot of the preview images (`Array.prototype.filter.call($uploadPreview.childNodes, …)`): a live NodeList shifts under removal-under-iteration, and the old `len--; i--;` compaction produced out-of-range `.tagName` TypeErrors that stayed crash-shadowed behind the earlier throw — snapshot any list a loop removes its own members from. The removal XHR still fires BEFORE any DOM removal (the preview DOM feeds the payload — preserve that ordering). The add-affordance restore is class-aware: the opt-in `data-gina-form-upload-hidden-class` is removed from the file input AND its parent (historical inline-`display` fallback kept), and the restore no longer aborts the removal pass. New `data-gina-form-upload-on-reset` / `-on-delete` callbacks — a bare identifier registered on `window`, the `-on-success` convention (function-call shapes warned + skipped) — fire ONCE per action AFTER the removal XHR with `{ $upload, bindingType, files }`, consumer throws contained. The documented `data-gina-form-upload-<reset|delete>-trigger` id override now resolves (its attribute name was built with a unary `+` coercion — NaN — so it could never match), and the trigger-not-found warn suggests the correct default id. Sibling guard: the form-level `clickProxyHandler` early-returns on a DETACHED click target — a node `.remove()`d during its own dispatch still bubbles to the form with `parentNode` null, so any delegated proxy dereferencing `event.target.parentNode` must tolerate self-removing targets. Browser-bundled → prod dist rebuild required. Tests: `test/core/validator-upload-reset-delete.test.js`.

228. **A multipart request with no successfully-parsed file part now reaches a terminal state — fields-only → resume, malformed → 400 (#B93/#B97, `0.5.15-alpha.2`).** `core/server.js`'s `multipart/form-data` branch drove the request-lifecycle continuation (`loadBundleConfiguration → handle`) ONLY from inside the per-file write-stream finish loop, and had NO `busboy.on('error')` handler — two unauthenticated DoS holes in the same block, both reachable because the body parse precedes routing AND all middleware (so ANY path, no auth, no log line at all). #B93: a well-formed FIELDS-ONLY body (busboy emits `finish` with zero write streams — measured against the vendored busboy) ran the finish loop zero times, so the continuation never fired and the request HUNG until a front-proxy timeout (the server sets `instance.timeout = 0`, so there is no server-side deadline). Fixed by extracting the continuation into `resumeAfterMultipart()` and calling it from a `if (total === 0) { resumeAfterMultipart(); return; }` branch in `busboy.on('finish')`; non-file fields stay dropped from `req.post` (the documented multipart limitation — reinstating them is a separate contract change, deliberately not coupled). #B97 (a #B30-sibling): a malformed / empty / non-multipart body labelled multipart makes busboy emit `error`, never `finish` — with no listener this became an uncaughtException → proc.js SIGTERM → single-request bundle KILL; fixed by adding `busboy.on('error')` → HTTP 400 with a `!response.headersSent && !request.handled` double-response guard. busboy always terminates in exactly `finish` XOR `error`, so the two handlers close every non-terminating path (no completion deadline needed). Rule: any stream/parser whose SUCCESS path drives a request's continuation must ALSO handle its error/empty terminals, or an unauthenticated malformed/empty body hangs or crashes the worker. Server-side only (no dist rebuild). Verified live (daemonless isolated boot: fields-only + unrouted → HANG→404, malformed → SIGTERM-crash→400 with the bundle surviving, with-file unchanged). Tests: `test/core/multipart-nonfile-terminal.test.js`.

229. **Form-associated custom elements (FACEs) now participate in FormValidator (#CC2, `0.5.15-alpha.2`).** Bind-layer widening in `core/plugins/lib/validator/src/main.js`: `getOwnedFaces()` collects hyphenated members of `form.elements` (the only hyphenated members a control collection holds are form-associated customs) + a `$faces` binding loop (auto-id `face.*`, dirty tracking, live-check); `registerForLiveChecking` detects a custom tag (`isCustomEl = tagName.indexOf('-')>-1`), widens its `input|textarea` gate, SKIPS the HTMLInputElement value-setter interception (`setObserver` — a FACE has its own `.value` accessor), and routes `addLiveForInput` with `isOtherTagAllowed=true` so the FACE live-checks on its composed bubbling `change` (caught by the existing form-level/reassociated change proxy — change-only, gina has no `input` proxy). Harvest/validate/serialize/error-render/Inspector-Forms already handled FACEs (name-keyed, tag-agnostic). GOTCHA the e2e caught (unit tests structurally cannot): a FACE reflects NEITHER element-level `.form` NOR `.name` (only `internals.form` + the attribute), so the `$faces` loop surfaces both — else the live-check path (`$el.form`/`$el.name`/`event.target.form`) throws and the whole form scan dies. Browser-bundled ⇒ prod dist rebuild. Author contract: `static formAssociated`, `name` attr, `.value` getter, composed `change` on commit.

230. **Multipart text fields are captured, and `send(FormData)` mixed payloads keep them — the full `send(FormData)`/multipart body contract (#B92 + its with-files sibling).** Client (`0.5.15` shipped the fileless half): the validator's `send(FormData)` splits entries — Files feed the hand-assembled multipart body, non-file fields are nested via `nestBracketNotationKey` (a byte-faithful `parseLocalObj` port) and JSON-posted when NO file is present, so `item[0][id]` arrives as `item: [ { id } ]` with values verbatim (#B92). Since the with-files fix: a MIXED FormData no longer drops its non-file fields — `buildMultipartFieldParts()` serializes them as standard multipart text parts (original bracket-notation names, RFC 7578 name escaping: CR/LF/double-quote percent-encoded) passed as `processFiles`' body accumulator, riding ahead of the file parts; files-only payloads are byte-identical (empty accumulator). Server (captures for EVERY multipart client — native HTML forms, curl, the gina client): a real busboy `'field'` listener now exists (busboy SKIPS all non-file parts when none is registered — attaching one is what flips capture on); it nests bracket names through the data helper's own nesting layer (`nestBracketNotationKey`, a framework global aliasing `parseLocalObj` — the same layer the urlencoded path uses) and exposes the fields as `request.body` + `request[method]` (POST/PUT/PATCH only — the GET/DELETE method slots feed URL params in the routing loop and are left alone) at the top of the busboy finish handler, before both dispatch paths. Values are VERBATIM — multipart part bodies are not url-encoded, so no decode and no `"true"`/`"false"`/`"on"`/`"null"` coercion (the JSON body contract, NOT the legacy urlencoded coercion — otherwise the same `send(fd)` call would change value TYPES depending on file presence); duplicate plain names last-wins. Caps, wired as busboy `limits` for the first time: `upload.maxTextFields` (default 1000) + `upload.maxTextFieldSize` (default 1MB, unit-aware like `maxFieldsSize`, explicit 0 = no limit) — excess fields (busboy emits `fieldsLimit` once then silently skips) or a truncated value (busboy truncates at the cap and flags `valueTruncated`) answer 400 instead of silent data loss. The client half is browser-bundled (validator `main.js`) → prod dist rebuild; the server half needs none.

231. **A routing rule's `param.title` now reaches `page.view.title` — the routing-param promotion loop in `setOptions()` was dead code since its introduction, and the route-name title is now the fallback it was always meant to be (#B98, `0.5.16-alpha.2`).** The historical generic `param.<key>` → `page.<key>` promotion loop in `core/controller/controller.js` `setOptions()` never executed its dispatch: it sat inside the inner `for..in` AFTER a `continue` that fires for every own enumerable property (a string enumerates its char indices), so `set()` was unreachable for any plain value — verified structurally identical in the pre-#P26 blob, so never a regression; the root of years of "`param.title`/`param.template`/`:param` promotions don't work" reports. The fix REPLACES the loop with a guarded title-only promotion (`typeof(p.title) == 'string' && p.title !== ''`) rather than reviving the generic dispatch, because measurement showed every other param key ALREADY reaches templates through live paths: `:bindings` + static keys land bulk-merged at `page.view.params.<key>` (with resolved URL values; `file`/`control`/`title` deliberately excluded from that merge), `section` at `page.section` (bespoke setter), `file` at `page.view.file` — `title` was the ONE promotion with no live equivalent, and a full revival would have created ~20 top-level `page.<key>` writes with zero framework readers plus collision landmines (a param named `data`/`view`/`environment`/`forms` would shadow a framework namespace before its setters run — worst case breaks the render-swig session block). Deliberately NO edit at the route-name write: `set()` merges TARGET-WINS (2-arg `merge` — an earlier write survives later fills), so the promotion simply running earlier in setOptions IS the fallback semantics (pinned by an ordering test); controller-set `data.page.view.title` still beats both via the render two-step merge. Rider: the `view:add` boilerplate layout read the never-populated `page.title`/`page.lang` — now `page.view.title`/`page.view.lang`, so scaffolded apps finally render a real tab title and lang attribute. Server-side only (controller.js is not browser-bundled — no dist rebuild); consumer pickup = version bump + bundle restart. Tests: `test/core/controller.test.js` §01–§03 (real-lib/merge replica + getter-instrument behavioral smoke + ordering pins + the dead-loop subtract control).

232. **The controller locale-DB fallback no longer crashes or falls back by accident — `region.isoShort` (the schema key) → legacy `region.shortCode` → `'en'`, every step guarded (#B100, 0.5.16).** Both catch sites — the `setOptions` locale bridge and the public-but-uncalled `getLocales()` — read `settings.region.shortCode` BLIND (a key the published settings schema forbids: `region` is `additionalProperties: false` with exactly `culture`/`isoShort`/`date`/`timeZone`, and nothing ever seeds it) and fed it unguarded into `findOne({lang: …}).content`. Three measured behaviours: (1) SCHEMA-VALID bundles (region present, no shortCode) did NOT throw — `Collection.find` round-trips its filter through `JSON.stringify`, which DROPS undefined-valued keys, so `findOne({lang: undefined})` collapses to a match-ALL and returns the FIRST record (`en`) while the warn printed ``replacing by default: `undefined` `` — a fallback by accident, not decision; (2) a bundle with NO `region` block threw at the warn's own deref (`reading 'shortCode'`); (3) a legacy `shortCode` naming an unloaded language threw on `.content` (the loaded set is the `core/locales/dist/region` files: `en` + `fr`). The throws escape `setOptions` synchronously and land in `router.route()`'s try/catch → a graceful per-request 500 via `throwError` — never a bundle kill. Fixed with a shared closure helper `getLocaleFallbackLang(conf)` (isoShort → shortCode → `'en'`, existence-guarded; `isoShort` is ISO 639-1, seeded by `bundle:add` as the culture's language part — this is its FIRST framework read) plus a guarded fallback lookup (`findOne(fallback) || findOne('en')`, `.content` gated, `[]` last resort) and the warn now printing the RESOLVED value. **Reusable gotcha: a `Collection` filter with an `undefined` value does not filter — JSON.stringify strips the key and the empty filter matches EVERY record; never pass a possibly-undefined criterion to `find`/`findOne` expecting a no-match.** Server-side only (controller.js not browser-bundled — no dist rebuild). Tests: `test/core/controller-locale-fallback.test.js` (source pins + a real-Collection/real-region-data replica + subtracts reproducing all three pre-fix behaviours); live-verified in an isolated daemonless boot (region-less bundle + unhandled lang → HTTP 200 + honest `en` warn, cold and warm).

233. **The global install died with EALLOWSCRIPTS when the npm 12 allow-scripts remedy was set — the nested framework install must not inherit the allowance (#B106, `0.5.17-alpha.2`).** npm exports every explicitly-set config value to lifecycle children as `npm_config_*` env vars, and npm rejects `allow-scripts` in PROJECT-scoped installs (`EALLOWSCRIPTS` — fires on npm 12.0.1 AND late npm 11.x, measured on 11.16/11.18, absent on 11.6): `script/post_install.js` `npmInstall()` chdirs into the framework dir and runs exactly such an install, so a user following the documented remedy (`--allow-scripts=gina`, or `npm config set allow-scripts=gina --location=user`) had the nested child die and the whole `npm install -g gina` fail — and on npm 12, where install scripts are BLOCKED by default and the flag is required, gina ≤ 0.5.16 had NO working install path at all (default → the bootstrap silently never runs: no `~/.gina`, no framework node_modules, no SUCCESS marker; remedy → the crash). Fixed with a save → delete → run-child → restore-if-defined guard on `npm_config_allow_scripts`, sibling to the pre-existing `npm_config_global` override at the same call site; the `typeof` gate on the restore is load-bearing (assigning `undefined` to a `process.env` key coerces it to the string `"undefined"`). Verified end-to-end in a node:26 container: the fixed package, published to a throwaway local registry and installed REGISTRY-SPEC with the remedy set, succeeds on npm 12.0.1 (SUCCESS + framework node_modules present, nested deps resolved) where `gina@0.5.16` fails on the same path. Three adjacent measurements worth keeping: (a) an `allowScripts` manifest field or a project `.npmrc` does NOT prevent the rejection — the inherited env var is refused regardless, so dropping the env var is the only working fix class; (b) npm 12 does NOT honor the name-keyed allowance for `file:`-tarball installs (scripts stay blocked with the user config AND the inline flag) — verify install-script fixes registry-spec (throwaway Verdaccio; `npm publish --tag` for prereleases), never from a packed tarball; (c) on npm ≤ 11 the allow-scripts warning is ADVISORY — scripts run with no flag, so the config is never needed there.

234. **Bundle-wide `sliding` / `maxAge` cache defaults — `writeCache` inherits them from `server.cache` (its `opt` arg) when a route omits them, mirroring the existing `cachingOption.ttl = opt.ttl` fallback (0.5.18-alpha.2).** The three render delegates each keep an INDEPENDENT `writeCache` copy — swig HTML (`controller.render-swig.js`), nunjucks HTML (`controller.render-nunjucks.js`), JSON responses (`controller.render-json.js`) — and all three already inherited `ttl` bundle-wide, so the `sliding`/`maxAge` fallback is added to all three IN LOCKSTEP (independent copies that silently diverge — a change to one must be mirrored in the others). Fallback shape, identical to `ttl`: `if ( typeof(cachingOption.X) == 'undefined' && typeof(opt.X) != 'undefined' ) cachingOption.X = opt.X` — FILL-only, so a per-route value always wins and an explicit route `sliding:false` overrides a bundle-wide `sliding:true`. No new downstream work: `lib/cache` `set()` already consumes `value.sliding`/`value.maxAge` (computes `expiresAt`, installs the sliding/ceiling timers), and the pre-existing `server.cache.sliding:false` template default makes the change a NO-OP for existing bundles (a route omitting sliding inherits `false` → identical to before; `opt.maxAge` absent → fallback inert). `core/template/conf/env.json` gains a `maxAge` key beside `server.cache.sliding` (both documented as bundle-wide defaults routes inherit; `maxAge:0` = no ceiling, only meaningful with `sliding:true`). NO config.js / schema change (the env-level `server.cache` is unvalidated; `schema/routing.json` already documents the per-route keys); server-side only — NO dist rebuild. Tests: `render-engine-dispatch.test.js §05e` (nunjucks source pin + behavioural (a)-(d) driving the REAL `writeCache`; (a)/(c) are the load-bearing subtract), `render-swig.test.js §22` + `render-json.test.js §05` (parity source pins). Orthogonal + unchanged: the dev-Inspector display metadata (`controller.js` `page.view.cacheType`/`cacheTTL`) has never surfaced sliding/maxAge (per-route or bundle).

235. **Pluggable render/output-cache backend strategy — `lib/render-cache` dispatcher + `server.cache.type` bundle-wide default (Slice 0, 0.5.18-alpha.2).** The memory/fs branch previously inlined in each render delegate's `writeCache` is extracted into ONE server-only dispatcher `lib/render-cache` (`RenderCache`, registered as `lib.RenderCache` via plain-require in `lib/index.js` — #B32-residual leaf-class rationale): `from(store)`, async `set(type, key, entry, {content,path,bundle,url,kind})` (memory → stamps `fromMemory`+inline `content`; fs → writes `<path>/<bundle>/<html|data><url>.<html|json>`, mkdirs the dir, stamps `filename`, registers a cleanupFn that rm-syncs the file on eviction; unknown/undefined type → no-op, exactly the pre-strategy behaviour), plus `has`/`get`/`delete`/`setEvents`/`invalidateByEvent`/`clear`/`stats` — all delegating to a wrapped `new Cache()`. The three render delegates (swig/nunjucks/json) and the isaac read path (`server.isaac.js`) now go through `renderCache.*` instead of touching `lib/cache` directly; render-swig KEEPS its own `cache` binding for the SEPARATE swig-compiled-template cache, and isaac KEEPS `cache` for the `/_gina/cache/stats` handler. NEW `server.cache.type` (template default `cache.type:"memory"`) is the bundle-wide default backend a route inherits when its `cache` block omits `type` (fill-only, mirrors the `ttl`/`sliding`/`maxAge` fallbacks; a per-route `cache.type` still wins; a route with no effective type stays uncached = unchanged; new bundles default to `memory`). **Load-bearing measurement — the whole render-cache arc (Slices 0-3) is SERVER-SIDE, NO dist rebuild: `lib/cache`'s AMD `define()` block is DORMANT** (`lib/cache` is not in the browser `build.json` `paths`, no browser src requires it, `invalidateByEvent`×0 in `dist/vendor/gina/js/gina.{js,min.js}`), so editing `lib/cache` — or the new server-only `lib/render-cache` — never touches the browser bundle. **Caveat for later slices:** the backing `serverInstance._cached` Map is MULTI-PURPOSE (also holds `swig:` compiled templates + `http2session:` sessions, classified by `stats()`), and `lib/cache`'s backing Map is a process singleton reassigned by `from()`, so a global `clear()` or a release-namespaced key must scope to the `static:`/`data:` output namespaces only. Tests: `test/lib/render-cache.test.js` (memory/fs/unknown/ttl-sliding-maxAge/events/clear/stats behavioural); the render delegate + dispatch source-pins now assert delegation to `renderCache.set(...)` (storage coverage moved to render-cache.test.js — the cmd-status-format extraction precedent).

236. **`helpers/context.js` `throwError` no longer crashes when called from a DETACHED context (cron/timer/worker/bootstrap) that holds a stale global `router` (0.5.18-alpha.2).** This is the GLOBAL helpers' error path (used by `getLib`/`getConfig`/context bootstrap) — distinct from the controller's `self.throwError(response, code, …)`. `core/router.js:484` stores each request's `{response, next, hasViews, isUsingTemplate}` in a GLOBAL context slot (`setContext('router', …)`) and NEVER clears it, and `throwError` (`context.js:284`) is its SOLE reader — so after any request finishes a stale routerObj lingers: a finished `response` (`headersSent === true`) and a non-callable `next`. A caller outside a live request (a `setTimeout` cron, a worker, a bootstrap-time `getLib()`) then entered the request-response branch and called the stale `next()` → `TypeError: next is not a function`, which additionally MASKED the real error it was reporting (e.g. the actual reason a cron's `getLib()` failed to load its lib — and the `getLib` inner catch even passes `isFatal=true` intending the emerg-log-and-return path, but pre-fix `isFatal` was honored ONLY in the no-router branch, so a stale router defeated it). Restructured into explicit guarded outcomes: render an error response only when a live response is still WRITABLE (`res && !res.headersSent`); hand back to the chain only when `next` is GENUINELY a function (`res && res.headersSent && typeof next == 'function'`); otherwise honor `isFatal` (`console.emerg` + return) or `throw err` — so a detached caller SURFACES the real error instead of crashing on a dead `next`, and the underlying failure becomes visible in the logs. All live-request behaviour is byte-identical (the always-JSON `isUsingTemplate = isUsingTemplate` self-assignment quirk — always `undefined`, so the HTML error-page branch is dead code — was deliberately PRESERVED; fixing it flips template-bundle error responses JSON→HTML, a separate behavioural decision). Because `throwError` is the router context's only reader, making IT robust fully covers all 6 call sites (bootstrap `:72`, getConfig `:437/:457`, getLib `:578/:583/:588`); clearing the router context per-request is a separate, higher-blast-radius hardening not needed for this class. Rule: any framework helper reachable from a non-request context (crons/timers/workers/bootstrap) must not assume a live `req`/`res`/`next` — the global `router` slot may be stale; gate `next()` on `typeof next == 'function'` and never write to a `headersSent` response. Server-side only — NO dist rebuild. Tests: `test/core/context-throwerror.test.js` (source pins + pure-logic replica + a subtract control reproducing the exact `TypeError`). Commit `6b08618d`, established 2026-07-14.

237. **`fs` render-cache backend now survives a restart — disk read-back on an index miss + a `<file>.meta` sidecar, absolute-expiry-preserving (Slice 1, 0.5.18-alpha.2).** The isaac read path was Map-ONLY, so after a restart `server._cached` is a fresh empty Map and every `fs`-cached file on disk was ORPHANED (never served, its cleanupFn never fired) — `fs` delivered no better cross-restart behaviour than volatile `memory`. `lib/render-cache` now does a disk fallback: `has(key)` is LENIENT (Map hit OR the body file exists) and `get(key)` is AUTHORITATIVE (Map hit → return; Map miss → read the entry back from the deterministic `<path>/<bundle>/<html|data><url>.<ext>` + its `<file>.meta` JSON sidecar, expiry-check, repopulate the Map, return). The sidecar (written at `set('fs')` time AFTER `mem.set`, so `meta.createdAt` == the `createdAt` lib/cache just stamped) carries `{createdAt, ttl, sliding, maxAge, visibility, responseHeaders}` — everything the isaac serve path replays. **ABSOLUTE EXPIRY IS PRESERVED (a restart never extends a TTL):** `mem.set` re-stamps `createdAt=now`, so the read-back passes an ADJUSTED remaining value — non-sliding `ttl := createdAt+ttl-now` (≤0 → miss + rm files), sliding keeps `ttl` (idle window restarts on the read-back access) but `maxAge := createdAt+maxAge-now` (the absolute ceiling; ≤0 → miss + rm); pure sliding (no maxAge) cannot judge the idle window from disk (lastAccess is not persisted) so a read-back is treated as a fresh access (documented restart imprecision). The disk-aware has/get is INERT unless a cache root is configured: the reader activates it via `renderCache.from(server._cached, options.cachePath)`, while the render delegates call `from(store)` with NO path — so their write-time `!renderCache.has(cacheKey)` gate stays Map-only (byte-identical). `options.cachePath` (reader) == `server.cache.path` (writer `opt.path`) by default — both resolve to the top-level `${cachePath}` (`${projectPath}/cache`, config.js alias); a project that overrides one independently must keep both on the same dir or read-back cannot find the files. `key → filename` parses on the FIRST two colons (`<static|data>:<bundle>:<url>`, url may hold `:` in a querystring); `static:`→html, `data:`→json; a single `fsPaths()` helper builds the write filename and the read-back filename so they cannot drift; cleanup rms the body + `.meta` together. Server-side only — NO dist rebuild (`lib/render-cache` server-only; `lib/cache`'s AMD `define()` dormant, #235). Scope: isaac serve (Express serve parity is an on-demand follow-up). Tests: `render-cache.test.js §07` (restart read-back recovery + a SUBTRACT proving a raw Map orphans the entry + expiry-preservation non-sliding/sliding + expired-drop + missing-sidecar → miss + inert-without-path).

238. **Release-namespaced render/output-cache keys — `renderCache.buildKey(kind, bundle, url)` centralizes the format + prepends a release token (Slice 2, 0.5.18-alpha.2).** The output-cache key format lived DUPLICATED at 4 sites (the 3 render delegates' write + the isaac reader's `keyPrefixes`) — the #C3 bundle-namespace bug was exactly such a writer/reader drift. `lib/render-cache` now owns the format in ONE `buildKey('static'|'data', bundle, url)` that all 4 call: it prepends `resolveReleaseToken()` = `getEnvVar('GINA_CACHE_NAMESPACE') || getEnvVar('GINA_VERSION') || ''` (sanitized to `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` → safe as BOTH a colon-delimited key segment and an fs path segment), producing `[<token>:]<kind>:<bundle>:<url>` (empty token → the flat pre-namespace format, back-compat). `GINA_VERSION` is set at runtime (`bin/gina-container:108`, `bin/cli:191`), so the DEFAULT namespaces caches by framework version → a framework upgrade auto-invalidates (a new build never serves a page rendered by old code); an operator sets `GINA_CACHE_NAMESPACE` (git SHA / build no) for per-deploy invalidation. **The token is ALSO an fs PATH segment** (`<cache.path>/<bundle>/<token>/<html|data><url>.<ext>`) — REQUIRED for correctness, not cosmetic: with the token only in the key, a namespace change reuses the SAME file path and Slice 1's read-back would serve stale cross-namespace content on the first post-upgrade request (measured). `parseFsKey` is token-aware (splits `[<token>:]<kind>:<bundle>:<url>`; a leading segment that is not `static`/`data` IS the token; url is the rejoined remainder so querystring colons survive); `set('fs')` derives the token FROM the key (via parseFsKey) so the write filename and the read-back filename (`fsBodyFor`, also key-derived) cannot drift, while bundle/kind/url stay payload-sourced (== the key's, by the delegate's own buildKey call). Scope: `static:`/`data:` output namespaces ONLY (never `swig:` compiled templates or `http2session:`). Old-namespace fs files orphan on disk until a cross-strategy flush (Slice 3) clears them; dev mode is unaffected (cacheless). Server-side only — NO dist rebuild. Tests: `render-cache.test.js §08` (buildKey precedence/version-fallback/sanitize + namespaced fs write+read-back + a cross-namespace INVALIDATION test proving relB never serves relA's bytes + parseFsKey round-trip); the nunjucks cacheKey source-pin + the §05e sandbox stubs (render-engine-dispatch.test.js) track the buildKey call.

239. **Native schema/DTO builder `lib/dto` (`require('gina').dto`) — JSON-Schema-canonical, three projections (#DTO1 primitive, 0.5.18-alpha.2).** Author a data shape ONCE: `dto.object({ email: dto.string().email().required(), age: dto.integer().min(0).max(120), role: dto.enum(['admin','user']).required() }).as('CreateUser')`. Projects to (a) dialect-aware JSON Schema — `.toJsonSchema('draft-07'|'2020-12'[,{standalone}])`, the IDENTITY/canonical form for OpenAPI 3.1 requestBody/responses + MCP inputSchema; (b) `.toRules()` — the LIVE form-validator rules-object (the SAME engine routing `validator::` + `forms/rules/*.json` use, so a DTO unifies validation rather than adding a parallel validator; measured returning `{isValid():fn, error:{field:{rule:msg}}, data:coerced}` with coercion + `exclude` stripping); (c) `.name` — stable id for the type generator + a route's `param.dto`. Curated vocabulary EXCLUDES `toFloat` (server crash, `form-validator.js:1514`) + `query` (spins a Controller). Zero runtime deps, CJS/`var`; named registry on `process.gina._dtos` (survives dev hot-reload — plain-`require`d in `lib/index.js` for stable `instanceof`). **⚠️ VALUE-RANGE (`.min()/.max()`) is SCHEMA-ONLY in this cut** — carried as `minimum`/`maximum` for OpenAPI/MCP fidelity but NOT runtime-enforced: the `is` evaluator (`form-validator.js:1115`) accepts only a single binary comparison (no `&&`, no `this.value`) and a `$field` self-ref CRASHES the server form-body path (`main.js:7166-7172` reads `$fields.count()` on the null server `$fields` — a #B85-sibling), so `toRules()` deliberately emits NO `$`; runtime value-bound = a follow-on (a first-class engine rule, browser-bundled → dist rebuild). **⚠️ A required field the client OMITS entirely PASSES** (isRequired fires only on present-but-empty, not a missing key) — a server-side validation driver MUST inject `''` for rule-declared fields absent from the payload before validating. Also un-collapses inline `validator::{...}` routing requirements into real JSON Schema via `lib.routingIntrospect.requirementToSchema()` (pure; the OpenAPI `.*` fix). Consumed by `bundle:openapi`/`bundle:mcp` (#DTO1c) + the default-on #DTO2 422 validation pipe (next). Server-side — NO dist rebuild. Tests: `test/lib/dto.test.js` (37, behavioural-through-the-real-engine + subtract) + `routing-introspect.test.js`.

240. **DTOs drive `bundle:openapi` + `bundle:mcp` schemas via a `dtos/<Name>.js` bundle convention (#DTO1c, 0.5.18-alpha.2).** A route declares `param.dto` / `param.responseDto` (names) in `routing.json`; the generators resolve each to `<bundle>/dtos/<name>.js` via `dto.load(bundleSrcPath, name)` — a new `lib.dto` method: require the file → `mod instanceof DtoObject ? mod : mod(dto)` (factory) → stamp+register → registry-fallback → null; fail-soft (a broken factory THROWS, the caller warns+skips), no `require.cache` eviction. **⚠️ A bundle DTO file MUST use the FACTORY shape `module.exports = function (dto) { return dto.object({...}, 'Name'); }`, NOT `require('gina').dto`** — because the OFFLINE `bundle:openapi`/`bundle:mcp` bootstrap via the lib registry (`bin/cli`), NOT `core/gna.js`, so a `require('gina')` inside a DTO file cold-loads gna.js with no bundle context and THROWS at `core/gna.js:174` (`ctxObj.paths` null). `require('gina').dto` works only at request-time in a booted bundle; the factory works in both (measured — the naive shape's offline throw was reproduced, the factory proven end-to-end). openapi (3.1 → JSON Schema 2020-12): `param.dto` on post/put/patch → `requestBody` + a `422`; `param.responseDto` → the 200 `content`. mcp (draft-07): `param.dto` → `inputSchema.body` on non-GET (else the lenient placeholder); `param.responseDto` → `outputSchema` (the runtime MCP server already passes it through). Both also un-collapse an inline `validator::{...}` URL-param requirement into a real schema fragment (the `.*`-collapse fix). Server-side/CLI-only — NO dist rebuild. Verified end-to-end against the real offline CLI (a scaffold bundle emitted a real requestBody / inputSchema.body / outputSchema / un-collapsed param). Tests: `test/lib/{bundle-openapi,bundle-mcp}.test.js` (source-pins + a source-locked replica through the real dto + introspect) + `dto.test.js §08` (dto.load).

241. **`helpers/context.js` `getLib`/`getConfig` no longer crash with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'conf')` on a PARTIAL Config (module-load / daemon-spawned bootstrap) — the resolver-layer sibling of the #236 detached-`throwError` fix (0.5.18-alpha.2).** `core/config.js` populates `envConf` (`Env.load`, `:391`) BEFORE `bundlesConfiguration` (assigned at `:243-250` only after `loadBundlesConfiguration` succeeds), and `bundlesConfiguration.conf` is an ALIAS of `envConf` (`:247` `conf: self.getInstance()`). When the async Config build ABORTS before completing — `config.js:223 if (err) { …; setTimeout(() => process.exit(1), 0); return; }` returns BEFORE the `:243` assignment (canonically a fail-closed `secrets.resolve` throws on an unset `${secret:KEY}` at `:2811`) — a detached caller (a bundle `onInitialize`, a cron, a bootstrap `getLib()`) observes a PARTIAL Config: `envConf` valid, `bundlesConfiguration` + `Config.initialized` undefined. `getLib` (`:600`) and both `getConfig` branches (`:465` with-confName, `:478` without) dereferenced `conf.bundlesConfiguration.conf[bundle][env]…` UNCONDITIONALLY there → the `reading 'conf'` TypeError → the #236 detached-path `throwError` re-threw → uncaughtException → SIGKILL, MASKING the real boot error. **Grep-PROVEN surface (not whack-a-mole):** a framework-wide grep of `bundlesConfiguration` reads (`core/ helpers/ lib/`, excl. dist) — the ONLY unguarded live consumers are `getLib` + `getConfig`; `config.js`'s own reads are guarded (`:3140 if (Config.initialized && self.bundlesConfiguration)`) or during-build; `lib/routing/src/main.js:1075` is commented-out (dead); 14/16 derefs are `.conf` (=== envConf). **Fix:** ONE shared `resolveBundlesConf(conf)` (`bundlesConfiguration.conf` when built, else the equivalent `envConf`, else null) consumed by `getLib` + BOTH `getConfig` branches so the two siblings cannot drift; PLUS fail-clean — `getConfig`'s two catches, `getLib`'s outer catch and its unresolvable-else all pass `throwError(…, isFatal=true)` (emerg-log + return, never a bare throw that escalates to SIGKILL). Byte-identical on the healthy path (bundlesConfiguration present); only the previously-crashing partial-Config path changes. **The partial Config is usually a SYMPTOM** — something upstream aborted the build (canonically a fail-closed `${secret:KEY}` resolution) — so hardening the resolvers UN-MASKS that real, actionable error (e.g. `Secret resolution failed for <KEY>`) instead of hiding it behind a `reading 'conf'` crash; the abort itself (e.g. secrets not wired for a deploy) is the caller's config to fix. Rule: a global config resolver reachable from a detached / module-load context must accept a partial Config (bundlesConfiguration may not be built yet; fall back to the aliasing envConf) and fail clean when neither source is usable. Server-side only — NO dist rebuild. Tests: `test/core/context-config-resolution.test.js` (source pins on the shared resolver + both resolvers routed through it + isFatal catches; full/partial/broken replicas; a subtract reproducing the exact crash pre-fix). Commit `b2dc67da`, established 2026-07-14.
